{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, the passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same story.","text":"The writer heard water in the kitchen.

They stood so quickly that the chair rolled back against the wall. The tap was still dry. Nothing moved in the sink. Yet the sound continued, thin and steady, as if it came from a room on the other side of the wall.

On the laptop, the boy set his suitcase upright.

“Someone’s washing their hands,” he said.

The woman shook her head. The sound below them stopped. In its place came three soft knocks.

The writer’s phone buzzed. Mara had sent a photograph of the building entrance, taken from the street. Beneath it she wrote, “I’m here. Is your front door open?”

The writer looked down the hall. They had locked it when they came home. They were almost sure.

“Don’t come up yet,” they typed.

A reply appeared at once. “I’m already upstairs.”

The knocks came again, this time from the apartment door. The writer crossed the hall and put a hand against it. Through the wood, Mara said their name.

They opened it. Mara stood there holding two paper cups, rain darkening the shoulders of her coat. She glanced past them toward the kitchen.

“Are you all right?”

“I think so,” the writer said.

From the laptop came the small clatter of suitcase wheels. They went back together. On the screen, the landing was empty. The stairwell door below stood open, and warm light fell across the first step.

Mara set down the cups. “Did they choose?” she asked.

The writer listened for the water. It was gone.

“Not yet,” they said."}
